scenes.text: Have you ever noticed that almost nothing in nature is actually blue, and that vibrant animals like the blue jay are actually tricking your eyes?

These beautiful creatures do not contain a single drop of blue pigment; instead, their feathers and wings have complex microstructures that physically bend light, reflecting only the blue wavelengths back to your eyes.

This mind-blowing biological hack is called structural color, and if you were to grind up a morpho butterfly's wing, the powder would instantly turn dull and brown because you destroyed the microscopic shape.

In fact, out of millions of species, only one single butterfly produces true blue pigment, so would you wear clothes made of light instead of dye, or do you prefer the illusion? Follow for more crazy secrets!
